messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated 5xx rate detected on inference-prod (route /v1/generate). Error spike started at 2026-03-14T21:10:02Z. P95 latency + error rate increased. Pager: Raj (oncall). Link: https://alerts.internal/INC-3129

Raj (oncall): ack — I'm on it. Creating an incident channel and taking first look.

Zoe (eng-runtime): jumping in. I'm seeing repeated segfaults in model-runner on gpu-34 with OOM traces and a recurring message: "kv_cache_async_flush: corrupted entry".

Marco (eng-sre): can you paste the tail of the runner logs from the host? quick grep would help.

Zoe (eng-runtime): here are the last few lines from gpu-34 (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-14T21:09:58Z] model-runner[pid=4123]: kv_cache_async_flush: flushing 4096 entries
[2026-03-14T21:09:59Z] model-runner[pid=4123]: ERROR: double free detected at 0x7f8a3c2b
[2026-03-14T21:09:59Z] model-runner[pid=4123]: segfault (signal 11)
[2026-03-14T21:10:00Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (model-runner) total-vm: 28G
[2026-03-14T21:10:01Z] kubelet: Pod inference/runner-gpu-34 terminated with exit code 139
```

Diego (prodops): Autoscaler is trying to replace pods but new pods hit the same segfault during init. So scaling doesn't help until the crash is mitigated.

Priya (support): CS reported one major customer complaining about a burst of 502s on embeddings endpoint ~21:10UTC. CS ticket CS-1249 created. Asking if we have a suggested workaround to share.

Raj (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic away from inference-prod to inference-backup (route weight change), 2) disable async kv-cache on runners, 3) roll restart affected pods with the disabled flag, 4) monitor for 5xx recovery and customer impact. I'll start traffic shift.

Marco (eng-sre): executing routing reweight -> POST to internal-router. Command:
```
curl -X POST https://router.internal/v1/reweight -d '{"from":"inference-prod","to":"inference-backup","pct":70}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```
response: {"status":"ok","from_pct":30,"to_pct":70} — routing changed. Monitoring 5xx.

Zoe (eng-runtime): quick hot mitigation: we can disable the async kvcache so flushes are synchronous and avoid the race. Flag is `--disable-async-kvcache`. Rolling restart with canary: 2 pods first.

Marco (eng-sre): performing canary restart on runner-deployment (namespace inference).
```
kubectl set env deployment/runner DISABLE_ASYNC_KVCACHE=true -n inference
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runner -n inference --record
```
healthcheck loop:
```
while true; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://inference-backend/health || echo fail; sleep 5; done
```

Marco (eng-sre): canary pods restarted, GPU pod gpu-34 rebooted and stayed up. No segfaults in the new logs. Memory usage stabilized on the canary.

Zoe (eng-runtime): logs on the restarted pod now show normal kvcache flushes without errors. Root cause hypothesis: race in async kv_cache flush under high prefix churn -> double-free -> segfault -> OOM cascade. I'll open a hotfix PR to add locking and validation.

Diego (prodops): after observing canary, I'm moving traffic back in 20% increments. Metrics at +20%: 5xx dropped ~85% from peak, p95 latency trending down.

Priya (support): updated CS-1249 with mitigation steps and ETA for permanent fix. Notified affected customers with suggested retries and a note that we're disabling async cache as temporary mitigation.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Pager handoff: Raj -> Marco for the next 30m.

Raj (oncall): Confirming 5xx returned to baseline and latency normalized. Closing immediate pager. We'll publish a short incident summary and follow up with a postmortem and hotfix timeline. :thumbsup:

Zoe (eng-runtime): next steps: open PR with targeted fix, put checksum/validation in kvcache flush path, add unit tests simulating high churn, and schedule a canary re-enable once patch lands.

Marco (eng-sre): I'll tag this incident for postmortem and add monitoring alert refinement to detect kvcache double-free patterns earlier.

Priya (support): Thanks — CS will monitor customer replies. Leaving ticket open until hotfix is deployed. :slightly_smiling_face:
